title: Etale local model uv=h of an at-worst-nodal family of relative dimension one
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], such that for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-geometric-point] the geometric fibre $X_\Omega=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is either empty or equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension], and each point of $X_\Omega$ at which $X_\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is not smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] has completed local ring isomorphic to $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Let $x\in X$ be a point at which $f$ is not smooth, i.e. a singular point of its fibre $X_s$, $s=f(x)$. Then there exist an etale morphism $V\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a global function $h\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, an etale morphism $U\to X$, a morphism $U\to V$ whose composite with $V\to S$ equals the composite $U\to X\to S$, and an etale $V$-morphism $U\to W$, where $W=V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[a]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[u,v,a]/(uv-a)=\operatorname{Spec}_V\mathcal O_V[u,v]/(uv-h)$ is the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] along the morphism $V\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[a]$ given by $a\mapsto h$, together with a point of $U$ mapping to $x$. Completion is maximal-ideal-adic [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and the two-variable power series ring is [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

source.place: Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family (hypothesis: at-worst-nodal of relative dimension 1, Tag 0C5A / Tag 0C59 (1))

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-noetherian-approximation] at $x$. Its hypotheses are exactly flatness, local finite presentation, and the geometric-fibre hypotheses here. It gives affine open neighbourhoods $X^\circ,S^\circ$, a Cartesian identification $X^\circ=X_0\times_{S_0}S^\circ$, and a flat finitely presented $f_0:X_0\to S_0$ between schemes of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, with the same geometric-fibre condition. The image $x_0$ of $x$ is nonsmooth for $f_0$. It is enough to construct the required diagram for $(f_0,x_0)$ and then pull it back, retaining a point over $x$ as in steps 8--9.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, first proof, first paragraph; Tag 0C5F (descent of the nodal condition)

proof.text: Write $s_0=f_0(x_0)$ and $k=\kappa(s_0)$. The fibre $C=(X_0)_{s_0}$ is a finite-type $k$-scheme: on a finite affine presentation cover its rings are $B_i\otimes_{R_i}k$, generated by the images of the finitely many generators of $B_i/R_i$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$, the fibre-product universal property identifies $C_\Omega$ with the geometric fibre of $f_0$ at the composite $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S_0$. By [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular], the first-Fitting singular locus is the nonsmooth locus and commutes with arbitrary base change; applying it to the fibre over $s_0$ shows that $x_0$ is nonsmooth on $C$. Thus [lem-trf-nodal-point-finite-separable-splitting] applies to $C,x_0$, giving a finite separable extension $K/k$ and a $K$-rational split node $x_K\in C_K$ above $x_0$, whose completed fibre ring is $K[[u,v]]/(uv)$.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, first proof, second paragraph; Tags 0CBT--0CBW

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-neighbourhood-prescribed-residue-field] to $S_0,s_0$ and $K/k$. It gives an étale pointed map $(V_1,v_1)\to(S_0,s_0)$ with $\kappa(v_1)=K$ over $k$. By the fibre-product universal property, $x_K$ gives a $K$-rational point $x_1$ of $X_1=X_0\times_{S_0}V_1$ above $v_1$, split in that fibre. Shrink $V_1$ to an affine neighbourhood of $v_1$ small enough to lie over an affine chart of $S_0$ on which its étale map has a finite presentation. This is possible by [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A finite presentation adds finitely many algebra generators, so the ring of this $V_1$ is a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra. The map $f_1:X_1\to V_1$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and locally finitely presented by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence].

source.place: Tag 0CBY, first proof, second paragraph and reduction to a finite-type base with split node

proof.text: The finite-type-over-$\mathbf Z$ scheme $V_1$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Its affine section ring $R_1$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. At $v_1$ with prime $\mathfrak p$, the stalk identification $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R_1,\mathfrak p}\cong (R_1)_{\mathfrak p}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification], together with [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], makes $A=\mathcal O_{V_1,v_1}$ Noetherian. Local finite presentation implies locally finite type by dropping the relations in its finite algebra presentation. We may therefore apply [lem-trf-formal-local-structure-nodal-family] to $f_1,x_1,v_1$. Flatness is step 3 and the split fibre node is $x_K$: under the identification $(X_1)_{v_1}\cong C_K$ of step 3, $x_1$ is $K$-rational, hence closed in that fibre, since in every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\ni x_1$ the map $B\to\kappa(x_1)=K$ is a surjective $K$-algebra map, so $x_1$ is a maximal ideal there and has no proper specialization (opens are stable under generization). It gives $\widehat h\in\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$ and a $\widehat A$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X_1,x_1}\cong\widehat A[[u,v]]/(uv-\widehat h)$, equivalently the completed local ring of $M_{\widehat h}$ at its origin.

source.place: Tag 0CBX and Tag 0CBY, first proof, third paragraph

proof.text: Set $T=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[a]$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[u,v,a]/(uv-a)$ over $T$. The ring map $\mathbf Z[a]\to\widehat A$, $a\mapsto\widehat h$, gives $\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A\to T$. Let $t$ be the image of its closed point and localize to obtain the local map $\sigma:\mathcal O_{T,t}\to\widehat A$. Form $Y_\sigma=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$. On rings, tensoring the displayed presentation replaces $a$ by $\widehat h$, so $Y_\sigma=M_{\widehat h}$. Let $y_\sigma$ be its origin and let $y\in Y$ be its image. The completed-model clause of [lem-trf-formal-local-structure-nodal-family] is exactly the $\widehat A$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X_1,x_1}\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y_\sigma,y_\sigma}$ required for relative approximation.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, first proof, third paragraph: the homomorphism sigma and the formal model Y_sigma

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-relative-completion-etale-approximation] to $X_1\to V_1$ and $Y\to T$, with $x_1,v_1,y,t,\sigma,y_\sigma$ just specified. Both bases are of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, both structure maps are locally finite type, and the isomorphism of completions is over $\widehat A$, as checked in steps 3--5. It gives an étale pointed map $(V_2,v_2)\to(V_1,v_1)$, a morphism $\tau:V_2\to T$, an étale $(U_0,u_0)\to(X_1,x_1)$, and an étale $V_2$-map $U_0\to Y\times_{T,\tau}V_2$. Put $h_2=\tau^*a\in\Gamma(V_2,\mathcal O_{V_2})$. Thus $Y\times_{T,\tau}V_2=\operatorname{Spec}_{V_2}\mathcal O_{V_2}[u,v]/(uv-h_2)$. This is the algebraic smoothing function supplied by approximation; it need not equal the original formal $\widehat h$.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, first proof, final paragraph; More on Morphisms Tag 0GDX (lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre)

proof.text: The map $X_1\to X_0$ is étale since it is the base change of $V_1\to S_0$, by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] now gives étaleness of $U_0\to X_1\to X_0$ and of $V_2\to V_1\to S_0$. Both triangles commute by the approximation theorem. We have obtained the required chart for $f_0$ and the chosen point $u_0$ maps to $x_0$.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, assembling the diagram for the finite-type model

proof.text: Define $V=V_2\times_{S_0}S^\circ$, $U=U_0\times_{X_0}X^\circ$, and pull back $h_2$ to a function $h$ on $V$. Since $X^\circ=X_0\times_{S_0}S^\circ$, associativity of fibre products identifies $U$ with $U_0\times_{S_0}S^\circ$ and gives $U\to V$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] makes $V\to S^\circ$ and $U\to X^\circ$ étale and preserves the étale map to $W=Y\times_TV$. The model square is Cartesian by its definition, and evaluation of its affine presentation gives $W=\operatorname{Spec}_V\mathcal O_V[u,v]/(uv-h)$. The open inclusions $X^\circ\to X$, $S^\circ\to S$ and their composites with these maps are étale by clauses (1)--(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation].

source.place: Tag 0CBY, first proof: pull the finite-type-model diagram back to the original affine base

proof.text: It remains to retain a point of $U$ over the originally prescribed $x$, rather than merely one over $x_0$. The field map $\kappa(x_0)\to\kappa(u_0)$ gives a surjective map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u_0)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x_0)$ because both spectra have one point. Its base change along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x_0)$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], hence has a point. By the residue-point maps and the fibre-product universal property this scheme maps into $U_0\times_{X_0}X^\circ=U$, and that point maps to $x$ in $X$. Together with steps 7--8 this proves every requested map, commutativity, étaleness and the point-existence clause.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, conclusion after base change; Morphisms Tag 01S1 (surjectivity under base change)

lean.statement: theorem exists_etale_nodal_local_model {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (hf : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (g : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S), IsEmpty (pullback (C := Scheme) f g) ∨ (Scheme.IsPureDimension (pullback (C := Scheme) f g) 1 ∧ ∀ z : pullback (C := Scheme) f g, ¬ ((geometricFiberProjection f Ω g).stalkMap z).hom.FormallySmooth → Nonempty (nodalCompletedLocalRing z ≃+* nodalPowerSeriesQuotient Ω))) (x : X) (hx : x ∉ f.smoothLocus) : ∃ (V U : Scheme.{u}) (h : Γ(V, ⊤)) (v : V ⟶ S) (uMap : U ⟶ X) (w : U ⟶ V) (m : U ⟶ pullback (nodalModelBaseMap) (nodalBaseMap h)), Etale v ∧ Etale uMap ∧ Etale m ∧ w ≫ v = uMap ≫ f ∧ m ≫ pullback.snd (nodalModelBaseMap) (nodalBaseMap h) = w ∧ ∃ z : U, uMap z = x
